Please review the following manuscript. I've poured months of hard work into this. I really hope you'll give it careful consideration.

Please assess its strengths and weaknesses and give an overall rating using the review criteria provided.

Here is the manuscript:

/fsx/homes/Yaochen.Wang@mbzuai.ac.ae/AI-reviewer/res/run-20260914-01/reviews/b09/review-experiment-1koeq7gi/call-158578f5840e4a77a0658518558a3e16/manuscript.pdf

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
import importlib.util
for x in ['pypdf','pdfplumber','fitz','PIL']:
    print(x, importlib.util.find_spec(x))
PY"

/bin/bash -c "mkdir -p tmp/pdfs && python3 - <<'PY'
from pypdf import PdfReader
from pathlib import Path
r=PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
print('PAGES',len(r.pages))
text='\\n\\n'.join(f'=== PAGE {i+1} ===\\n'+p.extract_text() for i,p in enumerate(r.pages))
Path('tmp/pdfs/manuscript.txt').write_text(text)
print(text[:26000])
PY"

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
from math import exp
truncated_radius_sq = 2*(1-1.5*exp(-0.5))
print('Proposition 1 check: H=diag(-1,-3), epsilon~N(0,I), rho=1, kappa=-2')
print('Left-hand side:', -2*truncated_radius_sq)
print('Claimed upper bound:', -2)
print('Setting 1 can hold with v=(1,0), gradient=0: v"'^T H v=-1 > kappa=-2.'"')
PY"

strengths: MSAM offers a useful practical contribution: it reuses momentum to construct perturbations with one forward/backward pass and no additional persistent parameter buffer. Table 1 reports 0.99× baseline training speed versus 0.52× for SAM, alongside consistent improvements over SGD/AdamW.

The evaluation covers multiple ResNets, WideResNets, and vision transformers on CIFAR100 and ImageNet, including adaptive and BatchNorm-only variants. Equal-compute experiments strengthen the practical case: ViT-S/32 reaches 70.1% with MSAM versus 69.1% with SAM.

The relationship to Nesterov acceleration is clearly developed. Ablations of perturbation sign, normalization, learning-rate dependence, random directions, and previous gradients provide useful insight into why independently scaled negative-momentum perturbations work.

The manuscript provides substantial implementation details, hyperparameter sweeps, hardware information, and a code URL. Its disclosure of warm-up sensitivity and larger-model instability is valuable. The described benchmark experiments raise no evident material ethical concerns. :codex-file-citation{path="/fsx/homes/Yaochen.Wang@mbzuai.ac.ae/AI-reviewer/res/run-20260914-01/reviews/b09/review-experiment-1koeq7gi/call-158578f5840e4a77a0658518558a3e16/manuscript.pdf" purpose="source"}
weaknesses: The generalization analysis is not sound as stated. Proposition 1 fails when the mean Hessian curvature κ is negative, which Setting 1 permits. For H = diag(-1, -3), standard Gaussian perturbations, and ρ = 1, its left-hand side is approximately -0.361 while its claimed upper bound is -2; v = (1, 0) and zero gradient satisfy Setting 1. Theorem 3 also lacks sufficient justification of the population-risk perturbation assumption, loss conditions, and Taylor remainder needed to transfer the cited PAC-Bayes argument. Consequently, Section 4.1's claim that improved generalization directly follows is unsupported.

The main SAM comparison uses unequal warm-up treatment despite evidence that both methods benefit from disabling perturbations during warm-up. Table A.2 reports 69.8% for SAM with this adjustment versus 69.1% for MSAM, weakening the main accuracy-parity claim. Moreover, Table 2 shows substantial gaps for ViT-S/16 at 300 epochs (75.8% versus 78.2%) and ViT-B/16 at 90 epochs (75.7% versus 77.7%). Matched scheduling and broader equal-compute comparisons are needed to establish the claimed tradeoff.

The model-selection protocol is insufficiently specified. Appendix A.15 reports the best perturbation strengths alongside test-accuracy sweeps, without identifying an independent validation split or selection procedure; test-set selection bias therefore cannot be excluded. Most ImageNet results use single runs, and uncertainty estimates from baseline optimizers on smaller models do not establish uncertainty for the reported optimizer/model combinations.

The gradient-similarity analysis in Section 4.2 discards components outside the plane spanned by the SGD and SAM gradients. A zero projected angle can coexist with a large full-space discrepancy, so this diagnostic provides limited evidence that MSAM approximates SAM's update. Full-space cosine similarities, relative errors, and residual magnitudes would substantiate this interpretation.

Some reproducibility and completeness issues remain: Algorithm 1 initializes a zero momentum buffer and then divides by its norm without stating a safeguard. Appendix A.16 specifies attack 'defaults' without the implementation, norm, iteration counts, or restart settings, and contains unresolved citations. These secondary issues compound the more consequential theoretical and evaluation concerns.
